- [x] Non-english title submitions will be closed directly ( 非英文标题的提交将会被直接关闭 ) ([Language Policy](https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow/issues/5910)).
- [x] Please do not modify this template :) and fill in all the required fields.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

```Markdown
Yes. The Upstage Go driver landed in #14817 with chat, list models, and check connection, but Embed (embeddings) is still a stub that returns "not implemented".

Upstage exposes an OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint at https://api.upstage.ai/v1/solar/embeddings via the solar-embedding-1-large family (solar-embedding-1-large-query for queries, solar-embedding-1-large-passage for passages). The Python side has had UpstageEmbed (extending OpenAIEmbed) in rag/llm/embedding_model.py:787 for a long time, but the Go layer has no embedding path for Upstage and the existing conf/models/upstage.json only lists chat models. A tenant who wants to use Upstage end to end (chat + embeddings) cannot currently run an embedding call in the Go layer.

Several other Go drivers already implement Embed (openai, ollama, lmstudio, mistral), so the rest of the codebase is ready to call into the driver. The Upstage driver is the missing piece.
```

### Describe the feature you'd like

Implement `UpstageModel.Embed` in `internal/entity/models/upstage.go` so the solar-embedding-1-large-* models work end to end.

The driver should:

- POST to `/v1/solar/embeddings` on the same base URL the chat path uses.
- Accept a model name and a list of input texts.
- Return a `[]EmbeddingData` with one vector per input, in the same order the inputs were given.
- Use the same HTTP client and the same shared transport that the chat path already builds.
- Use a per-call `context.WithTimeout` (the existing `nonStreamCallTimeout` constant) so a slow embedding call cannot block forever.

The `conf/models/upstage.json` file needs a small update so the driver can read the embeddings URL suffix from config:

  "url_suffix": {
    "chat": "chat/completions",
    "models": "models",
    "embedding": "embeddings"
  }

And two new entries under `models`:

  {
    "name": "solar-embedding-1-large-query",
    "max_tokens": 4000,
    "model_types": ["embedding"]
  },
  {
    "name": "solar-embedding-1-large-passage",
    "max_tokens": 4000,
    "model_types": ["embedding"]
  }

No new public API. No interface change. Just a real implementation behind an existing method.

### Describe implementation you've considered

_No response_

### Documentation, adoption, use case

```Markdown
No new docs are needed. Once the solar-embedding-1-large-* models are listed in conf/models/upstage.json, they will appear in the model picker the same way text-embedding-3-small does for OpenAI.

Use case: a tenant builds a knowledge base in RAGFlow and picks solar-embedding-1-large-passage as the embedding model. With this change, the Go layer calls https://api.upstage.ai/v1/solar/embeddings with the tenant's Upstage API key, gets real vectors back, and indexing works end to end.
```

_No response_

### Self Checks

- [x] I have searched for existing issues [search for existing issues](https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow/issues), including closed ones.

- [x] Please do not modify this template :) and fill in all the required fields.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

```Markdown
Yes. The Xinference Go chat provider is tracked in #14808, but the initial chat-provider scope leaves Rerank as a stub that returns "no such method".

Xinference supports rerank models through a dedicated `/v1/rerank` endpoint. The official docs describe a request shape with `model`, `query`, and `documents`, and the built-in model docs show rerank models are launched separately with `--model-type rerank`. That means RAGFlow should implement rerank only for Xinference rerank-capable models, without treating chat LLMs as rerankers.

Without this follow-up, a tenant can configure Xinference for chat in the Go layer but cannot use a Xinference-hosted rerank model to improve retrieval ranking.
```

### Describe the feature you'd like

Implement `XinferenceModel.Rerank` in `internal/entity/models/xinference.go` so rerank models served by a tenant's Xinference instance work end to end.

The driver should:

- POST to `/v1/rerank` on the normalized tenant-supplied Xinference base URL.
- Accept a model name / model UID, query string, and list of documents.
- Send the documented request shape: `model`, `query`, `documents`, and `top_n` when configured.
- Return a `RerankResponse` with each result's document index and relevance score.
- Validate response indices so duplicate or out-of-range indices fail clearly.
- Use the same optional-auth behavior as the chat provider: only set `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>` when a non-empty key is configured.
- Use a bounded non-streaming request timeout, matching the existing provider patterns.

The provider config should include the rerank suffix:

```json
"url_suffix": {
  "chat": "chat/completions",
  "models": "models",
  "embedding": "embeddings",
  "rerank": "rerank"
}
```

No new public API. No ModelDriver interface change. This is a follow-up implementation behind the existing `Rerank` method.

### Describe implementation you've considered

Follow the existing Go rerank implementations where possible, while preserving Xinference-specific behavior:

- normalize `http://host:9997` and `http://host:9997/v1` to the same `/v1` base before appending `rerank`;
- keep API key optional because default Xinference deployments run without auth;
- support the documented Xinference rerank request fields only;
- do not treat chat LLMs as rerank models, because Xinference launches rerank models separately with `--model-type rerank`.

### Documentation, adoption, use case

```Markdown
No new public RAGFlow API is required. Xinference's model list is dynamic because tenants launch their own models, so the config only needs URL suffix support.

Use case: a tenant runs Xinference locally, launches a rerank model such as bge-reranker-base or bge-reranker-v2-m3, and configures RAGFlow to use that model for retrieval reranking. With this change, the Go layer calls the real Xinference /v1/rerank endpoint and returns relevance scores to the retrieval pipeline.
```

### Additional information

Tracking issue: #14736
Xinference chat provider issue: #14808
Xinference rerank docs: https://inference.readthedocs.io/en/v1.6.1/models/model_abilities/rerank.html
Xinference built-in rerank models: https://inference.readthedocs.io/en/stable/models/builtin/rerank/

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

```Markdown
Yes. The Go rewrite of the RAGFlow model provider layer (tracked in #14736) does not yet have a driver for StepFun. The Python side has registered StepFun in rag/llm/__init__.py as a SupportedLiteLLMProvider with base URL https://api.stepfun.com/v1, and rag/llm/cv_model.py exposes StepFunCV (step-1v-8k) plus rag/llm/sequence2txt_model.py exposes StepFunSeq2txt (step-asr). But the Go layer has no case for "stepfun" in internal/entity/models/factory.go, so a tenant who configures StepFun as a model provider falls through to the default branch and gets the dummy driver. Chat, list models, and check connection all return "not implemented".

StepFun is one of the providers explicitly listed as unchecked on the umbrella issue #14736 and the link there points to https://platform.stepfun.com/docs/en/api-reference/chat/chat-completion-create. Its chat API is OpenAI-compatible (POST /v1/chat/completions, GET /v1/models), so the implementation pattern is the same as the merged OpenAI driver in #14605 and the merged Moonshot driver in #14433.
```

### Describe the feature you'd like

Add a Go driver for StepFun so that a tenant can configure StepFun as a model provider in the Go layer and run chat (streaming and non-streaming), list models, and check connection end to end.

Concretely:

- New file internal/entity/models/stepfun.go with a StepFunModel that implements the ModelDriver interface (NewInstance, Name, ChatWithMessages, ChatStreamlyWithSender, Embed, Rerank, ListModels, Balance, CheckConnection).
- internal/entity/models/factory.go: route the "stepfun" provider name to NewStepFunModel.
- New conf/models/stepfun.json with the public StepFun chat models (step-1-8k, step-1-32k, step-1-128k, step-1-256k, step-1-flash, step-2-16k, plus the step-1v vision family) and url_suffix entries for chat and models.

Method coverage in this PR:

- ChatWithMessages: POST https://api.stepfun.com/v1/chat/completions, same shape as moonshot, openrouter, openai.
- ChatStreamlyWithSender: SSE stream against the same endpoint with stream:true, same SSE-parsing pattern as the merged OpenAI streaming path.
- ListModels: GET https://api.stepfun.com/v1/models to list ids visible to the API key.
- CheckConnection: lightweight ListModels call to verify the API key.
- Embed: left as a stub returning "not implemented". StepFun has not advertised a public embeddings endpoint in the API reference linked from #14736, so any Embed implementation belongs in a separate follow-up only if/when the endpoint is verified, the same way the OpenAI driver staged it.
- Rerank: StepFun does not expose a rerank API, so this returns "no such method".
- Balance: StepFun does not expose a public balance API, so this returns "no such method".

No new public API. No interface change. The driver only adds a new case to the existing factory switch.

### Describe implementation you've considered

_No response_

### Documentation, adoption, use case

```Markdown
No new docs are needed. StepFun will appear in the model provider list once conf/models/stepfun.json ships, just like Moonshot, ZhipuAI, and DeepSeek already do.

Use case: a tenant builds a knowledge base in RAGFlow and picks step-1-32k as the chat model. With this change, the Go layer calls https://api.stepfun.com/v1/chat/completions with the tenant's StepFun API key and gets a real response, instead of the dummy driver "not implemented" error.
```

- Parse `results[].index` and `results[].relevance_score` from the response and copy them into the existing `RerankResponse{Data: []RerankResult{Index, RelevanceScore}}` shape that the rest of the codebase already consumes.
- Use the same HTTP client and the same shared transport that the chat path already builds.
- Use a per-call `context.WithTimeout` (the existing `nonStreamCallTimeout` constant) so a slow rerank call cannot block forever.
- Only set the Authorization header when a non-empty API key is supplied (same optional-auth pattern the chat and embeddings paths already use).

The `conf/models/localai.json` file needs a small update so the driver can read the rerank URL suffix from config:

  "url_suffix": {
    "chat": "chat/completions",
    "models": "models",
    "embedding": "embeddings",
    "rerank": "rerank"
  }

No new public API. No interface change. Just a real implementation behind an existing method.

Use case: a tenant runs LocalAI on a local server and has loaded a cross-encoder rerank model under the id "rerank-multilingual". With this change, the Go layer calls <tenant-url>/v1/rerank with that model id, the query, and the candidate documents, gets a sorted relevance_score array back, and the rerank stage of the RAG pipeline works end to end.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

The Go layer does not yet route the "xinference" provider name, so a tenant who configures Xinference falls through to the dummy driver instead of calling a running Xinference server.

Xinference provides OpenAI-compatible chat APIs through a configurable local or remote endpoint, for example http://127.0.0.1:9997/v1. In a default no-auth Xinference deployment, the OpenAI-compatible client still accepts an api_key value but it is not used by the server. When Xinference auth is enabled, requests should pass the configured API key as a Bearer token.
```

### Describe the feature you'd like

Add a Go driver for Xinference so that a tenant can configure Xinference as a chat model provider in the Go layer and use normal chat and streaming chat end to end.

Concretely:

- New tests in internal/entity/models/xinference_test.go.
- internal/entity/models/factory.go: route the "xinference" provider name to NewXinferenceModel.
- New conf/models/xinference.json with the provider metadata and representative chat model entries.

Initial method coverage:

- ChatStreamlyWithSender: same endpoint with stream:true and SSE parsing.
- ListModels: GET to the configured /v1/models endpoint when available.
- CheckConnection: lightweight model-list or minimal API probe to verify the configured base URL and optional API key.

### Describe implementation you've considered

Expected URL handling:

```

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

```Markdown
Yes. The Mistral Go driver landed in #14805 with chat, list models, and check connection, but Embed (embeddings) is still a stub that returns "not implemented".

Mistral exposes a public embeddings endpoint at https://api.mistral.ai/v1/embeddings with the `mistral-embed` model (1024-dimensional vectors, 8192 max input tokens). The Python side has had MistralEmbed in rag/llm/embedding_model.py for a long time, and the existing conf/models/mistral.json only lists chat models. A tenant who wants to use Mistral end to end (chat + embeddings) cannot currently run an embedding call in the Go layer.

Two other Go drivers already implement Embed (openai and ollama), so the rest of the codebase is ready to call into the driver. The Mistral driver is the missing piece for one of the providers explicitly listed as unchecked on the umbrella issue #14736.
```

### Describe the feature you'd like

Implement `MistralModel.Embed` in `internal/entity/models/mistral.go` so the `mistral-embed` model works end to end.

The driver should:

- POST to `/v1/embeddings` on the same base URL the chat path uses.
- Accept a model name and a list of input texts.
- Return a `[]EmbeddingData` with one vector per input, in the same order the inputs were given.
- Use the same HTTP client and the same shared transport that the chat path already builds.
- Use a per-call `context.WithTimeout` (the existing `nonStreamCallTimeout` constant) so a slow embedding call cannot block forever.

The `conf/models/mistral.json` file needs a small update so the driver can read the embeddings URL suffix from config:

  "url_suffix": {
    "chat": "chat/completions",
    "models": "models",
    "embedding": "embeddings"
  }

And one new entry under `models`:

  {
    "name": "mistral-embed",
    "max_tokens": 8192,
    "model_types": ["embedding"]
  }

No new public API. No interface change. Just a real implementation behind an existing method.

### Describe implementation you've considered

_No response_

### Documentation, adoption, use case

```Markdown
No new docs are needed. Once mistral-embed is listed in conf/models/mistral.json, it will appear in the model picker the same way text-embedding-3-small does for OpenAI.

Use case: a tenant builds a knowledge base in RAGFlow and picks mistral-embed as the embedding model. With this change, the Go layer calls https://api.mistral.ai/v1/embeddings with the tenant's Mistral API key, gets real vectors back, and indexing works end to end.
```

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

```Markdown
Yes. The Go rewrite of the RAGFlow model provider layer is tracked in #14736, and CometAPI is listed there as an unchecked provider. The Go layer does not yet route the "cometapi" provider name, so a tenant who configures CometAPI falls through to the dummy driver instead of calling the real CometAPI endpoints.

CometAPI exposes OpenAI-compatible chat and embeddings endpoints, plus a public model catalog and a separate quota query API. Adding a Go driver will let RAGFlow tenants use CometAPI from the Go API server for common chat and embedding workflows.
```

### Describe the feature you'd like

Add a Go driver for CometAPI so that a tenant can configure CometAPI as a model provider in the Go layer and use chat, streaming chat, embeddings, model listing, connection checks, and balance queries end to end.

Concretely:

- New file internal/entity/models/cometapi.go with a CometAPIModel that implements the ModelDriver interface.
- New tests in internal/entity/models/cometapi_test.go.
- internal/entity/models/factory.go: route the "cometapi" provider name to NewCometAPIModel.
- New conf/models/cometapi.json with CometAPI base URLs and representative chat / embedding models.

Initial method coverage:

- ChatWithMessages: POST https://api.cometapi.com/v1/chat/completions.
- ChatStreamlyWithSender: same endpoint with stream:true and SSE parsing.
- Embed: POST https://api.cometapi.com/v1/embeddings.
- ListModels: GET https://api.cometapi.com/api/models.
- CheckConnection: lightweight model-list or minimal API probe to verify the key / network path.
- Balance: GET https://query.cometapi.com/user/quota?key=... using CometAPI's query service.
- Rerank: return "no such method" unless a documented CometAPI rerank endpoint is confirmed.
- TranscribeAudio / AudioSpeech / OCRFile: return "no such method" unless docs clearly confirm support and response shape.

No new public RAGFlow API. No ModelDriver interface change. The driver only adds a new provider implementation and a factory switch case.

### Describe implementation you've considered

Follow the existing OpenAI-compatible provider patterns in the Go layer, especially OpenAI / OpenRouter / Mistral, while handling CometAPI-specific endpoints separately:

- base model API: https://api.cometapi.com/v1
- public model catalog: https://api.cometapi.com/api/models
- quota query service: https://query.cometapi.com/user/quota

### Documentation, adoption, use case

```Markdown
No new user-facing docs are required for the initial driver. CometAPI will appear in the model provider list once conf/models/cometapi.json ships.

Use case: a tenant builds a knowledge base in RAGFlow and picks a CometAPI-backed chat or embedding model. With this change, the Go layer calls CometAPI's real endpoints with the tenant's API key instead of returning the dummy driver error.
```

### Self Checks

- [x] I confirm that I am using English to submit this report ([Language Policy](https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow/issues/5910)).
- [x] Non-english title submitions will be closed directly ( 非英文标题的提交将会被直接关闭 ) ([Language Policy](https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow/issues/5910)).
- [x] Please do not modify this template :) and fill in all the required fields.

### RAGFlow workspace code commit ID

b8522ed67

### RAGFlow image version

b8522ed67

### Other environment information

```Markdown
- **Files affected:**
  - `api/apps/restful_apis/user_api.py` (lines 124, 386, 531, 840)
  - `api/db/db_models.py` (lines 158–163, 707–723)
- **Python:** 3.10–3.12
- **Severity:** Critical — every successful authentication response leaks the user's bcrypt password hash and raw `access_token` to the client

---
```

### Actual behavior

Every endpoint that returns user data calls `user.to_json()` or `current_user.to_dict()`, which resolves to `self.__dict__["__data__"]` — a raw dump of **every column** in the `User` database row. The `User` model includes sensitive fields `password` (bcrypt hash) and `access_token` (the raw UUID secret that the JWT wraps), both of which are sent verbatim in the JSON response body.

**Four endpoints are affected:**

### 1. `POST /users/login` (line 124) — password hash + stale access_token leaked

```python
response_data = user.to_json()
user.access_token = get_uuid()
# ...
return await construct_response(data=response_data, auth=user.get_id(), message=msg)
```

`to_json()` is called **before** the access_token is rotated, so the response contains the **previous** access_token (which was valid until this moment) alongside the password hash.

### 2. `GET /users/me` (line 386) — password hash + current active access_token leaked

```python
return get_json_result(data=current_user.to_dict())
```

This endpoint returns the **currently active** access_token on every call. Any authenticated request to this endpoint exposes the live secret.

### 3. OAuth callback (line 531) — password hash leaked for new OAuth registrations

```python
return await construct_response(
    data=user.to_json(),
    auth=user.get_id(),
    message=f"{nickname}, welcome aboard!",
)
```

### 4. Password reset (line 840) — newly set password hash leaked immediately

```python
return await construct_response(data=user.to_json(), auth=user.get_id(), message=msg)
```

The user's brand-new password hash is returned in the response the instant they reset their password.

---

### Expected behavior

1. The `password` field (bcrypt hash) must **never** appear in any API response. Exposing the hash enables offline brute-force attacks without triggering rate limits.
2. The `access_token` field must **never** appear in any API response. The raw `access_token` UUID is the secret signed into the JWT via `URLSafeTimedSerializer`. Leaking it allows an attacker to forge valid authentication tokens indefinitely — surviving password changes and logouts.
3. All user-facing endpoints should return only non-sensitive fields (id, nickname, email, avatar, language, etc.).

---

### Steps to reproduce

```Markdown
### Reproducing password hash + access_token leak on login

1. Register a user account (or use an existing one).
2. Log in via `POST /users/login` with valid credentials.
3. Inspect the JSON response body.
4. **Result:** The response `data` object contains `password` (bcrypt hash, e.g. `$2b$12$...`) and `access_token` (raw UUID) fields.


curl -X POST http://localhost/users/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email": "user@example.com", "password": "<encrypted_password>"}'


Response (truncated):

{
  "code": 0,
  "data": {
    "id": "abc123...",
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "nickname": "User",
    "password": "$2b$12$XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
payload.title: [Bug]: User Credentials (Password Hash + Access Token) Leaked in Login API Response via `to_json()`/`to_dict()`

payload.body:
## Feature Description

Currently, RAGFlow Agents do not support tagging or labeling functionality. As users create more Agents, managing and organizing them becomes increasingly difficult. Tag-based management would allow users to categorize and filter Agents efficiently.

## Expected Behavior

- Users can assign one or more tags to an Agent (e.g., "customer-support", "internal", "finance", "experimental")
- The Agent list view should support filtering by tag
- Agents can be sorted by tag, or grouped by tag in the UI
- Tags should be editable and removable from the Agent settings
- Tag metadata should be searchable across the Agent list

## Use Case

- Teams with many Agents (20+) need a way to organize them by function, team, or purpose
- Quick filtering to find Agents relevant to a specific workflow or project
- Batch operations on Agents sharing the same tag (e.g., bulk enable/disable)
- Simplifies Agent governance in large-scale deployments

## Additional Context

This is a common organizational feature in most agent or bot management platforms. Tag support would significantly improve usability for power users and enterprise deployments.

payload.author: caesergattuso
payload.body:
## Feature Description

Currently, Pipeline and Agent are separate modules in RAGFlow. Users who want to leverage Pipeline features (e.g., chunking strategies, document preprocessing, classification) within an Agent workflow must manage these as two distinct steps outside of RAGFlow.

It would be valuable to expose Pipeline capabilities directly inside the Agent module, so that when a file is uploaded through an Agent, it can be processed through Pipeline-style chunking and preprocessing strategies — without performing vectorization — and then fed into Agent tools/modules for further handling.

## Expected Behavior

- When a file is uploaded in an Agent session, users can apply Pipeline chunking strategies (e.g., "by title", "by section", "recursive", etc.)
- Chunking occurs without vectorization at this stage — purely structural document processing
- The processed chunks are then available to Agent modules for:
  - Tool invocation (e.g., lookup, summarization, extraction)
  - Context injection
  - Structured output generation
- This bridges Pipeline preprocessing and Agent execution in a single flow

## Use Case

- Users want to upload a document, pre-chunk it using advanced strategies, and then have the Agent reason over those chunks without full vectorization overhead
- Combining structured document parsing (Pipeline) with LLM-based reasoning (Agent) in one workflow
- Scenarios where only a subset of chunks need to be vectorized or where chunking strategy should be decoupled from embedding

## Additional Context

This would make Agent much more powerful for document-heavy workflows, reducing the need to run separate Pipeline jobs before Agent interactions. It also gives users fine-grained control over how documents are split before Agent processing, rather than being locked into a single chunking method.
payload.title: [Feature Request] Enable Pipeline capabilities inside Agent - pre-chunking without vectorization for Agent processing

payload.author: caesergattuso
payload.body:
## Feature Description

Currently, RAGFlow Pipelines allow creating a single custom node (e.g., "Categorize by Title"). However, users need the ability to define multiple custom nodes within a single Pipeline to handle different classification logics in sequence.

## Expected Behavior

- Users should be able to add multiple custom nodes in a Pipeline workflow
- For example, a Pipeline could have:
  - Node 1: "Classify by Document Title (Category A)"
  - Node 2: "Classify by Document Title (Category B)"
- Each node should have its own configuration (e.g., different keywords, thresholds, or output routing)
- Nodes can be arranged sequentially or in parallel to form a more flexible workflow

## Use Case

- Handling multi-stage classification where documents need to be routed based on different criteria
- Building complex decision trees within a single Pipeline (e.g., Title → Department → Priority)
- Reducing the need to create multiple separate Pipelines for related but distinct classification tasks

## Additional Context

This would significantly enhance the flexibility of Pipeline workflows, especially for enterprise use cases where a single document may need to be evaluated against multiple classification rules in one flow.
payload.title: [Feature Request] Support multiple custom nodes in Pipeline - e.g., multiple title-based classifiers

## Feature Description

When users retrieve relevant chunks from a RAGFlow knowledge base, the search results currently return the chunk content and metadata, but do not provide a direct way to download or access the original source file. Users need the ability to obtain a downloadable URL or file path for the document that the chunk belongs to.

## Expected Behavior

- When a chunk is returned from a search, the API response should include a reference to the source document
- A downloadable URL (e.g., /api/v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/documents/{document_id}/download) should be accessible or derivable from the chunk metadata
- The frontend UI should offer a "Download File" or "View Source" option for each chunk result

## Use Case

- Users perform a semantic search and want to access the full original document from which a chunk originated
- Integrating RAGFlow retrieval results into external workflows that require the original file
- Auditing or reviewing source documents in full after seeing relevant chunk excerpts

## Additional Context

This is particularly relevant for document sets where only a specific chunk is relevant. The ability to download the full source file completes the retrieval loop and enables end-to-end document workflows.

- **Scope**: REST `chat_api` / `search_api` in this tree; not claimed as duplicate of a specific upstream issue (local code review; contrast with already-hardened `agent_api` in the same product).

### Actual behavior

Any authenticated user can pass arbitrary `owner_ids` query parameters on **`GET /chats`**. The handler forwards them directly into `DialogService.get_by_tenant_ids` without verifying that each ID is a tenant the caller is allowed to see.

The database filter is effectively:

`dialog.tenant_id IN (supplied owner_ids) OR dialog.tenant_id == current_user.id`

(see `get_by_tenant_ids` in `dialog_service.py`). There is **no join or membership check** tying `owner_ids` to the caller’s teams/tenants.

The post-query line in `list_chats` only restricts rows to `chat["tenant_id"] in owner_ids`; it does **not** prove the user may query those tenants. An attacker who knows (or guesses) another user’s tenant UUID (the `tenant_id` stored on dialogs, same as owner scope elsewhere) receives that tenant’s chat list in the JSON response.

The list path builds each item with `_build_chat_response`, which exposes rich dialog fields from the ORM row (including `llm_setting`, `prompt_config`, similarity / vector weights, `rerank_id`, resolved dataset names via `kb_ids`, etc.). That is a **cross-tenant configuration and knowledge-base linkage leak**, not merely chat titles.

**Same pattern** exists on **`GET /searches`**: unvalidated `owner_ids` → `SearchService.get_by_tenant_ids` with the same “filter to requested tenants only” list comprehension and no authorization gate. Impact is somewhat lower than chats (different projection), but tenant-scoped metadata is still exposed.

**Inconsistency**: `GET /agents` already validates `owner_ids` against an authorized set derived from joined tenants and rejects unknown IDs (`list_agents` in `agent_api.py`). Chats and searches never applied that pattern.

### Expected behavior

- `owner_ids` must be intersected with (or validated against) the **same authorized tenant set** used elsewhere (e.g. pattern in `list_agents`: build `authorized_owner_ids` from membership, then `requested - authorized` → error; pass only authorized IDs into `get_by_tenant_ids`).
- If the client requests any `owner_ids` not in the authorized set, return an explicit error (mirroring agents: message like “Only authorized owner_ids can be queried.” and appropriate `RetCode`).
- Optional follow-up: add regression tests modeled on `test_agents_webhook_unit.py` → `test_agents_crud_unit_branches` (unauthorized `owner_ids` rejected; authorized path passes expected tenant list into the service).

2. As user **A**, obtain **B**’s tenant identifier used as `tenant_id` on dialogs (same UUID used as owner scope in multi-tenant APIs; e.g. from a legitimate shared-team context, support export, or another leak — the bug is that **any** value is accepted without membership).
3. As **A**, call:

### RAGFlow workspace code commit ID

### RAGFlow image version

nightly (main @ e46989832)

### Other environment information

```Markdown
- Component: Python backend (Quart) — api/apps/restful_apis/document_api.py
- Affected endpoint: GET /api/v1/documents/images/<image_id>
- Auth decorator on route: none (no @login_required, no tenant scoping)
- Introduced by: PR #14344 (migration of /v1/document/thumbnails → /api/v1/thumbnails and /v1/document/image → /api/v1/documents/images)
```

### Actual behavior

While reading through `api/apps/restful_apis/document_api.py` I noticed the `/documents/images/<image_id>` route at line 1641 has **no decorator at all** — no `@login_required`, no tenant scoping. Every other route in this file is gated by `@login_required` (lines 58, 121, 246, 366, 612, 966, 1116, 1229, 1357, 1428, 1540, 1690, 1740, 1860, 1893). There is also no global `before_request` hook adding auth anywhere under `api/` (verified with grep).

The handler splits the user-supplied `image_id` on `-` and passes the two halves straight to the storage backend:

```python
arr = image_id.split("-")
if len(arr) != 2:
    return get_data_error_result(message="Image not found.")
bkt, nm = image_id.split("-")
data = await thread_pool_exec(settings.STORAGE_IMPL.get, bkt, nm)
response = await make_response(data)
response.headers.set("Content-Type", "image/JPEG")
return response
```

So anyone on the internet can pull arbitrary `(bucket, key)` pairs out of MinIO/S3/OSS with `curl`, no session required. Two things make this strictly worse than ordinary thumbnail leakage:

1. The thumbnail bucket and the raw-document bucket are the **same bucket**. `api/db/services/file_service.py:487` writes the original PDF/Word/etc. blob with `STORAGE_IMPL.put(kb.id, doc.location, blob, kb.tenant_id)`, and line 519 writes the thumbnail with `STORAGE_IMPL.put(kb.id, thumbnail_location, img)`. The `image/JPEG` Content-Type is hardcoded, so a request for `<kb_id>-report.pdf` will return the **raw PDF body** mislabeled as JPEG.
2. The application itself embeds the vulnerable URL into authenticated list responses at `document_api.py:734` and `document_api.py:1221` as `f"/api/v1/documents/images/{kb_id}-{thumbnail_filename}"`. So `(kb_id, filename)` pairs flow into HTML, browser history, server access logs, and Referer headers — and any one of those can be replayed by an unauthenticated attacker.

The `len(image_id.split("-")) != 2` guard is effectively a no-op for the realistic attack surface: 32-hex KB ids are hyphen-free, and corporate filenames like `report.pdf`, `invoice.docx`, `Q3.xlsx` are hyphen-free.

This is the same threat model PR #14625 / commit d51fb8857 just patched for `GET /v1/document/get/<doc_id>` — except this endpoint is strictly worse because it doesn't even require authentication, and isn't restricted to image-typed files.

This is a separate but related vulnerability with a different attack surface … It should be addressed in a follow-up."* That follow-up was never filed, and PR #14344 then migrated the route into `restful_apis/document_api.py` carrying the

payload.body:
## Summary

The RAGFlow codebase uses Quart (async Flask) but contains widespread violations of idiomatic asyncio patterns. Fire-and-forget tasks, event-loop nesting anti-patterns, thread-pool saturation from sync tool calls, and mixed sync/async HTTP stacks are pervasive across `api/`, `rag/`, and `agent/` directories. This RFC proposes a structured remediation plan targeting the highest-risk issues first.

> **Important correction to initial draft**: Agent tools (`SearXNG`, `TuShare`, etc.) that use synchronous `requests` inside `_invoke` are **not** directly blocking the Quart event loop. The `invoke_async` path in `agent/tools/base.py:165-182` dispatches sync `_invoke` calls through `thread_pool_exec(...)`, so they run on a thread pool. The real issues are **thread-pool saturation**, **cancellation latency**, and **mixed sync/async HTTP stacks** — not event-loop starvation per se. See Finding 1b below.

---

## Motivation

Non-idiomatic asyncio code causes:

1. **Silent task failures** — `asyncio.create_task()` without storage or await means failures go undetected and the GC may collect the task before it completes.
2. **Thread-pool saturation** — sync blocking calls (e.g., `requests`) competing for the shared thread pool degrades throughput under concurrent load.
3. **Runtime crashes** — calling `loop.run_until_complete()` inside an already-running event loop raises `RuntimeError: This event loop is already running`.
4. **Debugging difficulty** — mixed sync/async code makes stack traces untrustworthy and race conditions hard to reproduce.

RAGFlow is a long-running service; these issues compound under load.

---

## Scope

**In scope:**
- All Python files under `api/`, `rag/`, and `agent/` that contain `async def` functions
- Tool classes invoked from Quart route handlers or `agent/canvas.py`

**Out of scope:**
- `web/` frontend (JavaScript/TypeScript, different concurrency model)
- `deepdoc/` document processing (CPU-bound, intentionally sync)
- Test files (separate cleanup track)

---

## Findings

### Finding 1a — Fire-and-forget `create_task()` in API routes (High)

**Severity**: High
**Files affected**: 2

```python
# api/apps/restful_apis/tenant_api.py:100-107
asyncio.create_task(send_invite_email(...))
# No await, no storage — failure silently swallowed, task may be GC'd
```

```python
# api/apps/restful_apis/agent_api.py:1706
asyncio.create_task(background_run())  # fire-and-forget
```

**Problem**: Unobserved tasks can fail silently. The task object going out of scope before completion means the garbage collector may clean it up prematurely, or exceptions may be lost.

**Fix**: Either `await` the task directly (if fire-and-forget is acceptable), or store the returned `asyncio.Task` in a collection (e.g., `self._background_tasks`) and handle failures via `task.add_done_callback()`.

> **Note**: `api/utils/api_utils.py:777-788` was incorrectly cited in the initial draft. The pressure test code at that location **does** store tasks in a list, awaits them via `asyncio.gather()`, and explicitly cancels all tasks on exception. This is correctly structured and does **not** exhibit the fire-and-forget anti-pattern. Removed from this finding.

---

### Finding 1b — Sync HTTP calls in agent tools via thread pool (Medium)

**Severity**: Medium
**Files affected**: ~6 agent tools + 2 API service files

Agent tools (`SearXNG`, `TuShare`, `GitHub`, `QWeather`, `PubMed`) use the synchronous `requests` library. These are dispatched via `thread_pool_exec(...)` in `agent/tools/base.py:182`, so they do **not** directly block the Quart event loop. However, they still cause:

- **Thread-pool saturation**: concurrent sync HTTP calls compete for thread pool threads, degrading throughput under load.
- **Cancellation latency**: long-running HTTP requests (e.g., 10s timeout) cannot be canceled promptly until the underlying `requests` call completes or times out.
- **Inconsistent HTTP stack**: `api/` services and `agent/` tools use `request

# Python 3.12 → 3.13 Version Bump

## 1. Motivation

Python 3.13 (October 2024) brings significant improvements for RAGFlow's I/O-bound async workload:

- **Free-threading** (PEP 703): No GIL — notable throughput gains for document processing pipeline
- **Improved error messages** with color tracebacks
- **New deprecations** that RAGFlow should stay current with

RAGFlow currently pins `requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.15"` in `pyproject.toml`. This RFC proposes bumping the floor to 3.13 across all surfaces.

---

## 2. Scope

### 2.1 Files to Update

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `pyproject.toml:8` | `requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.15"` → `">=3.13,<3.15"` |
| `Dockerfile:81` | `uv python install 3.12` → `3.13` |
| `Dockerfile:150` | `uv sync --python 3.12 --frozen` → `3.13` |
| `.github/workflows/tests.yml:161` | `uv sync --python 3.12 --frozen` → `3.13` |
| `.github/workflows/tests.yml:225` | `uv sync --python 3.12 --frozen` → `3.13` |
| `CLAUDE.md:121` | `Python 3.10-3.12` → `Python 3.10-3.13` |
| `uv.lock` | Regenerated with `uv lock --python 3.13` |

### 2.2 Out of Scope

- Dependency version bumps (only Python version floor changes).
- Base Docker image changes (not pinned to a specific Python minor version).
- `docker-compose-base.yml` service images (managed separately).

### 2.3 Lockfile Regeneration (Required, Not Optional)

The `uv.lock` file **must be regenerated** as part of this change — there is no post-merge CI job that does this. The frozen lockfile is used directly by `uv sync --frozen` in:

- `Dockerfile:150`
- `tests.yml:161`
- `tests.yml:225`

---

## 3. Risk Assessment

### 3.1 Compatibility Risk: **HIGH**

Most packages are safe — they declare no `<3.13` upper bound. The primary risk is a hard blocker from `graspologic`.

### 3.2 Package Audit Summary

| Package | Status | Notes |
|---------|--------|-------|
| Most dependencies | ✅ Safe | No `<3.13` upper bound |
| `graspologic` | ❌ **BLOCKS 3.13** | `requires-python = ">=3.9,<3.13"` — hard blocker |
| `onnxruntime-gpu` | ⚠️ Verify | Need to confirm py313 binary wheel exists |
| `strenum` | ⚠️ Monitor | Deprecated, no `requires-python` declared |

Full audit table in [docs/proposals/python-313-upgrade.md](docs/proposals/python-313-upgrade.md).

### 3.3 Critical Blocker: graspologic

**`graspologic`** (`git+https://gitee.com/infiniflow/graspologic.git@38e680cab72...`) is directly imported in first-party graph RAG code:

```
rag/graphrag/general/entity_embedding.py:13: import graspologic as gc
rag/graphrag/general/leiden.py:11: from graspologic.partition import hierarchical_leiden
rag/graphrag/general/leiden.py:12: from graspologic.utils import largest_connected_component
```

Its `pyproject.toml` declares `requires-python = ">=3.9,<3.13"` — it will refuse to install on Python 3.13 under any circumstances.

### 3.4 Resolution Path (Recommended Order)

| Option | Approach | Effort |
|--------|----------|--------|
| **A. Fork & patch (recommended first move)** | Fork graspologic, remove `<3.13` cap, retag; update `pyproject.toml:48`; regenerate `uv.lock`; run graph-rag smoke test. | Medium |
| **B. Local API replacement (fallback if A fails at runtime)** | Replace the narrow API surface in `leiden.py:11-12` and `entity_embedding.py:13` with an alternative or stdlib equivalent. | Medium |
| **C. Full-package vendoring (last resort)** | Only if A and B both fail due to distribution or governance reasons. | High |

---

## 4. Implementation Notes

### 4.1 PR Structure

Single PR containing:
1. All 6 version-pinning file changes (`pyproject.toml`, `Dockerfile`, `tests.yml`, `CLAUDE.md`)
2. Regenerated `uv.lock` from a clean `uv lock --python 3.13` run
3. graspologic resolution (fork & patch, per option A above)

### 4.2 Pre-Merge Verification Commands

```bash
# 1. Check no 3.12 references remain in codebase
grep -rn "3\.12" --include="*.py" --include="*.yml" --include="*.toml" --include="*.md" . | grep -v ".git" | grep -v "node_modules"

# 2. Dry-run uv sync

# Flask/Quart → FastAPI Migration Feasibility Assessment

## 1. Current State Overview

### 1.1 Framework Distribution

| Area | Framework | Scale |
|------|-----------|-------|
| Main API (`api/`) | **Quart** (async Flask) | 26 files, ~10k lines |
| Admin Panel (`admin/server/`) | **Flask** | 7 files, ~2.2k lines |
| **Total** | — | 33 files, ~12.2k lines |

### 1.2 File Distribution

```
api/apps/                          # Main API (Quart)
├── __init__.py                   # 343 lines - app factory + blueprint loading
├── llm_app.py
├── backward_compat.py
├── dify_retrieval.py
├── doc.py (sdk)
├── session.py (sdk)
└── restful_apis/                 # Core REST API
    ├── agent_api.py             # 1,892 lines ⬅ largest
    ├── document_api.py          # 1,895 lines
    ├── chat_api.py             # 1,130 lines
    ├── dataset_api.py            # 810 lines
    ├── user_api.py               # 842 lines
    ├── file_api.py               # 376 lines
    ├── connector_api.py          # 531 lines
    ├── chunk_api.py              # 445 lines
    ├── search_api.py             # 216 lines
    ├── system_api.py             # 421 lines
    ├── mcp_api.py                # 331 lines
    ├── memory_api.py             # 304 lines
    ├── openai_api.py             # 300 lines
    ├── task_api.py               # 101 lines
    ├── plugin_api.py             # 30 lines
    ├── stats_api.py              # 55 lines
    ├── file2document_api.py      # 176 lines
    ├── langfuse_api.py            # 99 lines
    └── tenant_api.py             # 163 lines

admin/server/                     # Admin Panel (Flask)
├── admin_server.py               # 83 lines
├── routes.py                     # 691 lines
├── auth.py                       # 242 lines
├── services.py                   # 723 lines
├── config.py                     # 338 lines
├── roles.py                      # 76 lines
├── responses.py                  # 32 lines
├── models.py                     # 15 lines
└── exceptions.py                 # 16 lines
```

---

## 2. Key Technical Dependencies

### 2.1 Flask/Quart-Specific Dependencies

| Dependency | Purpose | Migration Difficulty |
|------------|---------|---------------------|
| `quart_cors` | CORS middleware | ⚠️ Medium - FastAPI has built-in CORSMiddleware |
| `quart_auth` | `Unauthorized` exception only | ⚠️ Medium - custom auth implemented in `__init__.py:95-193` |
| `quart_schema` | OpenAPI schema generation | ✅ Low - FastAPI has native support |
| `itsdangerous.URLSafeTimedSerializer` | Token minting/parsing (NOT JWT) | 🔴 High - not JWT; existing tokens incompatible with JWT swap |
| `flask_login` | Admin login (admin) | 🔴 High - no direct replacement |
| `flask_session` | Server-side sessions (admin) | 🔴 High - no built-in support in FastAPI |

### 2.1.1 Auth Architecture (Corrected)

The main API does **not** use `quart_auth`'s `login_required` or `current_user` implementations. Those are **custom-built** in `__init__.py:95-193`:

- `login_required` decorator → custom implementation wrapping `quart_auth.Unauthorized`
- `current_user` → `LocalProxy` reading from `g.user` via custom `_load_user()`
- `quart_auth` is only still used for the `Unauthorized` exception import

**Actual migration task**: Port custom token lookup and auth wrappers, not replace `quart_auth` end-to-end.

# Proposal: Replace Peewee with SQLModel

> **Status**: Draft
> **Date**: 2026/05/10
> **Author**: RAGFlow Team

---

## 1. Background and Goals

RAGFlow's backend currently uses [Peewee](https://docs.peewee-orm.com/) as its ORM. The core database abstraction lives in [api/db/db_models.py](api/db/db_models.py) and [api/db/db_utils.py](api/db/db_utils.py). Over time, we have identified structural pain points that cannot be resolved without migrating to a more capable ORM.

We propose migrating directly to [SQLModel](https://sqlmodel.tiangolo.com/).

**Why SQLModel over raw SQLAlchemy**: SQLModel is built by the FastAPI author on top of SQLAlchemy and Pydantic. It allows table models and API data models to **share field definitions through inheritance**, reducing boilerplate without conflating persistence and API contracts. For a project like RAGFlow with many Pydantic schemas, shared base classes cut down on field duplication while keeping DB-only fields out of API contracts. Under the hood, SQLModel exposes the full SQLAlchemy Engine/Session API, so all session lifecycle, connection pooling, and retry mechanisms are identical to raw SQLAlchemy.

---

## 2. Known Pain Points

### 2.1 Nested Connection Context Collisions

**Problem**: The codebase extensively uses `@DB.connection_context()` decorators to manage database connection contexts.

Current usage locations (partial):

| File | Lines | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `api/db/services/common_service.py` | 89, 109, 139, ... | Batch insert operations |
| `api/db/services/user_canvas_version.py` | 41, 61, 78 | User canvas version operations |
| `api/db/services/langfuse_service.py` | 35, 45, 55 | Langfuse integration |
| `api/db/services/mcp_server_service.py` | 35, 81, 90 | MCP server management |
| `api/db/services/search_service.py` | 42, 56, 82, 119 | Search service |

When business logic forms nested call chains:

```
parent_function()        # @DB.connection_context()
  └─ child_function()   # @DB.connection_context()
       └─ grandchild_function()  # @DB.connection_context()
```

A child-layer `connection_context()` may reopen a connection already held by the parent, or return it to the pool prematurely due to exception mishandling, ultimately triggering `InterfaceError: (0, '')` or connection leaks.

**Root cause**: Peewee's connection context is "flat" — the decorator decides on its own whether a connection is already open, making reference counting and state machine behavior unpredictable under nesting.

### 2.2 Scattered Manual Connection Management

Beyond decorators, there are explicit `db.connect()` / `db.close()` calls:

- [agent_api.py:808-809](api/apps/restful_apis/agent_api.py#L808-L809) — manual open/close in `test_db_connection`
- [apps/__init__.py:340](api/apps/__init__.py#L340) — `_db_close(exception)` in global exception handler

These scattered connection management sites lack consistency and are difficult to audit.

### 2.3 Temporary Patches for Lost Connections

To cope with `InterfaceError` and `Lost connection` (MySQL error codes 2013/2006), the project implemented a custom `RetryingPooledMySQLDatabase` at [db_models.py:260](api/db/db_models.py#L260):

```python
class RetryingPooledMySQLDatabase(PooledMySQLDatabase):
    def execute_sql(self, sql, params=None):
        # catches (OperationalError, InterfaceError) and retries
```

This indicates that Peewee's native connection pool cannot reliably handle disconnects, requiring business-layer workarounds.

### 2.4 Unclear Session Lifetime

In Peewee, connection open/close is spread across decorators and middleware, with no unified authority controlling "one request = one connection." This makes the following scenarios difficult to model:

- Long-running tasks that need to explicitly release connections mid-flight
- Connection isolation between concurrent requests
- Precise control over transaction boundaries

---

## 3. How SQLModel Addresses These

SQLModel is built on two proven libraries:

- **SQLAlch

### Actual behavior

After upgrading from v0.24.0 to v0.25.x, some dialogs trigger the following 
validation error when accessed:

  hint: 101 Field: <tenant_rerank_id> - Message: <Input should be a valid string> - Value: <9>

This happens because:
1. `tenant_rerank_id` is defined as `IntegerField` in `api/db/db_models.py` 
   (lines 749 and 990)
2. The column is therefore created as INT in MySQL
3. Dialogs created when a rerank model was configured stored the integer 
   primary key from `tenant_llm` table (e.g. 9) into this column
4. The Pydantic schema in v0.25 now validates `tenant_rerank_id` as a string
5. The automatic migration at startup only fixes NULL/empty values — it cannot 
   update rows containing integer values because it doesn't recognize them as 
   invalid

Root cause confirmed by inspecting db_models.py inside the running container:

  # line 749 and 990
  tenant_rerank_id = IntegerField(null=True, help_text="id in tenant_llm", index=True)

And confirmed in MySQL:
  SELECT id, name, tenant_rerank_id FROM dialog WHERE tenant_rerank_id REGEXP '^[0-9]+$';
  → returns dialogs with tenant_rerank_id = 9 (integer stored in an INT column)

  ALTER TABLE dialog MODIFY COLUMN tenant_rerank_id VARCHAR(255) NULL;
  → fails: "Incorrect integer value: 'bge-reranker-v2-m3-Q8' for column 'tenant_rerank_id'"
  → confirms the column is INT in the DB

### Expected behavior

`tenant_rerank_id` should be defined as `CharField` in db_models.py to store 
the model name as a string (e.g. "bge-reranker-v2-m3-Q8"), consistent with 
how `rerank_id` is defined on line 748/989 and how the Pydantic API validates it.

Fix in api/db/db_models.py:
  # line 749 and 990 — change from:
  tenant_rerank_id = IntegerField(null=True, ...)
  # to:
  tenant_rerank_id = CharField(max_length=255, null=True, ...)

The automatic migration should also handle the INT → VARCHAR type change and 
convert any existing integer values to the corresponding model name by joining 
with the tenant_llm table.

### Steps to reproduce

```Markdown
1. Install RAGFlow v0.24.0 with at least one tenant that has a rerank model configured
2. Create one or more chat assistants (dialogs) — they will store the integer 
   FK from tenant_llm as tenant_rerank_id
3. Upgrade to v0.25.x
4. Access any chat assistant that was created in step 2
5. Observe: hint: 101 Field: <tenant_rerank_id> - Message: <Input should be a valid string> - Value: <9>
```

### Additional information

Startup logs confirm the migration runs but updates 0 rows:
  Found 5 empty tenant_rerank_id dialogs.
  Update 0 tenant_rerank_id in table dialog.

The migration only targets NULL/empty values, not integer values.

The integer value (9) was the primary key of a row in tenant_llm that has since 
been deleted and recreated (explaining the gap in auto-increment IDs: 8 → 10).

Workaround:
  ALTER TABLE dialog MODIFY COLUMN tenant_rerank_id VARCHAR(255) NULL;
  ALTER TABLE tenant MODIFY COLUMN tenant_rerank_id VARCHAR(255) NULL;
  UPDATE dialog SET tenant_rerank_id = 'bge-reranker-v2-m3-Q8'
  WHERE tenant_rerank_id = '9' AND tenant_id = '<your_tenant_id>';

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

```Markdown
Yes. The NVIDIA Go driver in internal/entity/models/nvidia.go has a stub Rerank method that always
returns "no such method", even though the NVIDIA NIM platform hosts dedicated reranking models:

  - nvidia/nv-rerankqa-mistral-4b-v3
  - nvidia/llama-3.2-nv-rerankqa-1b-v2

accessible via:

  POST https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/ranking

Note that NVIDIA NIM exposes reranking under /v1/ranking (not /v1/rerank). The request shape is
also different from other providers: the query is a {"text": "..."} object and each passage is a
{"text": "..."} object inside a "passages" array, not a plain string array. The response returns a
"rankings" array with {"index": N, "logit": F} entries that must be sorted by index before
returning scores in the original input order.

The conf/models/nvidia.json file has no "rerank" URL suffix and no rerank models listed, so even
if Rerank worked the picker would have nothing to select.

ListModels and CheckConnection are already implemented in this driver. Rerank is the natural next
step. NVIDIA NIM is one of the most commonly used GPU-accelerated inference platforms, so a
working reranker is high value for RAG pipelines running on NVIDIA hardware.
```

### Describe the feature you'd like

Implement `NvidiaModel.Rerank` in `internal/entity/models/nvidia.go` so NIM reranking models work
end to end, and add the rerank model entries and URL suffix to `conf/models/nvidia.json`.

The driver should:

- POST to `${BaseURL}/${URLSuffix.Rerank}` (resolves to
  `https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/ranking` with default config).
- Send `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`, the same header the chat path already uses.
- Build the NVIDIA-specific request body:
  ```json
  {
    "model": "<model_name>",
    "query": {"text": "<query_text>"},
    "passages": [
      {"text": "<passage_0>"},
      {"text": "<passage_1>"}
    ],
    "truncate": "END"
  }
  ```
- Parse the `rankings` array from the response, sort entries by `index`, and return a `[]float64`
  of `logit` scores in the original input order.
- Use a per-call context deadline so a slow rerank call cannot block forever.

The NVIDIA NIM ranking response shape to parse:

```json
{
  "rankings": [
    {"index": 0, "logit": 4.75},
    {"index": 1, "logit": 2.10}
  ]
}
```

`conf/models/nvidia.json` needs two updates:

1. Add the `"rerank"` URL suffix:

```json
"url_suffix": {
  "chat": "chat/completions",
  "models": "models",
  "rerank": "ranking"
}
```

2. Add the rerank model entries:

```json
{
  "name": "nvidia/nv-rerankqa-mistral-4b-v3",
  "max_tokens": 4096,
  "model_types": ["rerank"]
},
{
  "name": "nvidia/llama-3.2-nv-rerankqa-1b-v2",
  "max_tokens": 4096,
  "model_types": ["rerank"]
}

the rerank models to the picker and wires the existing Rerank stub to a real implementation.

They want to use nvidia/nv-rerankqa-mistral-4b-v3 to rerank retrieval results before passing them

the tenant's NIM API key, gets back relevance scores, and the retrieval pipeline works end to end

always returns "not implemented", even though the Moonshot (Kimi) platform exposes an
OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint at:

  POST https://api.moonshot.cn/v1/embeddings

and provides a dedicated embedding model:

  - moonshot-v3-embedding (max 128,000 tokens — large context window well-suited for long
    documents)

However, conf/models/moonshot.json currently lists no embedding models and has no "embedding" URL
suffix defined, so even if Encode worked the model picker would show nothing to select.

The Moonshot driver already implements Balance, ListModels, CheckConnection, and both chat methods.
The pattern for Encode is well-established by the SiliconFlow, ZhipuAI, Aliyun, and OpenAI
drivers. Moonshot is the gap: a tenant who wants a fully Moonshot-native RAGFlow stack (chat +
embeddings from the same provider) is blocked at the embedding step.

Moonshot's embeddings endpoint accepts the same OpenAI-compatible request shape (model + input
array), so the implementation maps directly onto the pattern the other drivers already use.
```

Implement `MoonshotModel.Encode` in `internal/entity/models/moonshot.go` so
`moonshot-v3-embedding` works end to end, and add the embedding model entry and URL suffix to
`conf/models/moonshot.json`.

- POST to `${BaseURL}/${URLSuffix.Embedding}` (resolves to

```json
"url_suffix": {
  "chat": "chat/completions",
  "models": "models",
  "balance": "users/me/balance",
  "embedding": "embeddings"
}
```

2. Add the embedding model entry:

```json
{
  "name": "moonshot-v3-embedding",
  "max_tokens": 128000,
  "model_types": ["embedding"]
}
```

No new public API. No interface change. The Aliyun and OpenAI Encode implementations are a good
reference since all three providers use the same OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint shape.

```Markdown
No new docs are needed. Moonshot is already listed in the model provider picker. This issue just
adds the embedding model to the picker and wires the existing Encode stub to a real implementation.

Use case: a tenant builds a long-document knowledge base in RAGFlow and wants to use Moonshot for
both chat and embeddings from a single provider. moonshot-v3-embedding's 128K token context window
makes it particularly well-suited for embedding long documents without chunking. With this change,
the Go layer calls https://api.moonshot.cn/v1/embeddings with the tenant's API key, gets real
vectors back, and indexing works end to end without switching providers.

OpenAI-compatible shape used by most other providers:

  Request body uses `texts` (not `input`) and requires a `type` field ("db" for document
  indexing, "query" for search queries). The CN endpoint (api.minimaxi.com) also requires
  a GroupId passed as a URL query parameter: ?GroupId=<group_id>. The response returns a
  top-level `vectors` array (not OpenAI's `data[].embedding` shape), and error status is
  indicated by `base_resp.status_code` (0 = success).

The conf/models/minimax.json file currently has no "embedding" URL suffix and no embedding models
listed, so even if Encode worked the model picker would have nothing to select.

The MiniMax driver already implements ListModels, CheckConnection, and both chat methods. The Encode
gap means a tenant who wants to use MiniMax for a full RAG stack (chat + embeddings from the same
provider and API key) is blocked at the embedding step.
```

### Describe the feature you'd like

Implement `MinimaxModel.Encode` in `internal/entity/models/minimax.go` so `embo-01` works end to
end, and add the embedding model entry and URL suffix to `conf/models/minimax.json`.

The driver should:

- POST to `${BaseURL}/${URLSuffix.Embedding}` (resolves to
  `https://api.minimaxi.com/v1/embeddings` for the CN region with default config).
- For the CN endpoint, append `?GroupId=<group_id>` as a URL query parameter (the group ID is
  already available in `APIConfig`).
- Send `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`, the same header the chat path already uses.
- Build the MiniMax-specific request body:

```json
{
  "model": "embo-01",
  "type": "db",
  "texts": ["text one", "text two"]
}
```

  Use `type: "db"` when embedding documents for storage and `type: "query"` when embedding a
  search query. For RAGFlow's use case (indexing document chunks), `"db"` is the correct type.

- Parse the MiniMax-specific response:

```json
{
  "vectors": [
    [0.03016241, 0.03617699, ...],
    [0.01234567, ...]
  ],
  "model": "embo-01",
  "total_tokens": 12,
  "base_resp": {
    "status_code": 0,
    "status_msg": "success"
  }
}
```

  Check `base_resp.status_code == 0` for success. Return `[][]float64` from the top-level
  `vectors` array, preserving input order.

- Use a per-call context deadline so a slow embedding call cannot block forever.

`conf/models/minimax.json` needs two updates:

1. Add the `"embedding"` URL suffix:

```json
"url_suffix": {
  "chat": "v1/text/chatcompletion_v2",
  "models": "v1/models",
  "tts": "v1/t2a_v2",
  "files": "v1/files/list",
  "embedding": "v1/embeddings"
}
```

2. Add the embedding model entry:

```json
{
  "name": "embo-01",
  "max_tokens": 4096,
  "model_types": ["embedding"]
}
```

Note: Because MiniMax uses a non-standard format, this implementation cannot follow the generic
OpenAI-compatible Encode pattern. It requires a custom request builder and a custom response
parser, similar to how the MiniMax chat implementation uses a non-standard path and body.

### Other environment information

```Markdown
- Component: Go model driver
- Provider: Google / Gemini API
- SDK: google.golang.org/genai
- OS type: Any
```

### Actual behavior

`GoogleModel.CheckConnection` always returns `no such method`, even when the configured Google AI Studio / Gemini API key is valid and `GoogleModel.ListModels` can successfully call the Google GenAI SDK.

This makes the Google provider connection check fail incorrectly. It also means the check does not surface real Google API errors, such as disabled API, invalid key, or permission errors.

Separately, `GoogleModel.ListModels` dereferences `apiConfig.ApiKey` without first validating that `apiConfig` and `ApiKey` are present, so missing credentials can fail with a nil pointer dereference instead of a normal validation error.

### Expected behavior

`GoogleModel.CheckConnection` should perform a real lightweight connectivity check, matching the behavior used by other Go model drivers.

Expected behavior:

- With a valid Gemini API key, `CheckConnection` should succeed.
- With an invalid key or disabled Gemini API, `CheckConnection` should return the underlying Google API error.
- With nil or empty API key configuration, `ListModels` / `CheckConnection` should return a normal validation error instead of panicking.
- `ListModels` should return all available model names from the Google GenAI SDK model listing response.

### Steps to reproduce

```Markdown
1. Configure the Google model provider with a valid Google AI Studio / Gemini API key.
2. Trigger the provider connection check, or call the Go driver directly:

   model := &models.GoogleModel{}
   apiConfig := &models.APIConfig{ApiKey: &apiKey}
   err := model.CheckConnection(apiConfig)

3. Observe that the connection check returns `no such method`.
4. Call `model.ListModels(apiConfig)` with the same key.
5. Observe that model listing can use the Google GenAI SDK, while the connection check still fails because it is hardcoded.
```

### Additional information

The fix is to delegate `GoogleModel.CheckConnection` to `GoogleModel.ListModels`, add nil/empty API key validation, and keep returning Google SDK errors directly so connection-check failures reflect the real provider response.

Validation from the fix branch:

- `go test -count=1 ./internal/entity/models`
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/entity/models`
- Live Google AI Studio check: `CheckConnection` succeeded and `ListModels` returned 50 models.

```Markdown
Note: this issue was originally filed for Aliyun Balance. After verifying that the
DashScope endpoint specified in that earlier framing returns 404 (it does not exist
on DashScope, and account balance is exposed only via the separate BSS OpenAPI which
uses AccessKey + HMAC-SHA256 signing rather than the model API key), I am repurposing
this issue for a different concrete gap in the same Go-driver track.

The VolcEngine Go driver in internal/entity/models/volcengine.go ships a stub
ListModels method that always returns "volcengine, no such method". Other Go drivers
that have already landed in the recent Go-rewrite effort (DeepSeek, Gitee, NVIDIA,
OpenAI, SiliconFlow) all implement ListModels against the OpenAI-compatible /models
endpoint, and the model picker UI relies on it.

VolcEngine (Doubao / Ark) does expose a documented OpenAI-compatible models endpoint
that accepts the same Bearer token used for chat and embedding requests:

  GET https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com/api/v3/models

Without ListModels, a tenant who configures VolcEngine has no in-product way to see
which endpoints are available on their Ark account, even though the chat and
embedding paths in the same driver are already working.

conf/models/volcengine.json also does not yet declare a "models" entry under
url_suffix, so even if the method body were filled in there is no URL to call.
```

### Describe the feature you'd like

Implement `VolcEngine.ListModels` in `internal/entity/models/volcengine.go` and add the
matching `models` URL suffix to `conf/models/volcengine.json` so the existing model
picker works for VolcEngine the same way it already works for the other drivers in this
package.

The driver should:

1. Resolve the region with a default-region fallback, the same way the surrounding
   VolcEngine methods already do.
2. GET `${BaseURL[region]}/${URLSuffix.Models}`, which resolves to
   `https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com/api/v3/models` with the default region.
3. Send `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>` when an API key is configured. Mirror the
   existing NVIDIA `ListModels` behavior of omitting the header when the key is empty,
   so an unauthenticated caller still gets a clear `401 Unauthorized` from upstream.
4. Surface non-200 responses with the upstream status line and body, the same shape
   the other Go drivers use.
5. Parse the JSON response via the package-level `DSModelList` / `DSModel` types
   already used by DeepSeek, Gitee, and SiliconFlow, and return the list of model ids
   in input order. When the response includes `owned_by`, render the entry as
   `id@owned_by`, matching the convention of the other drivers.

`conf/models/volcengine.json` needs the `"models"` URL suffix added alongside the
existing `chat`, `files`, and `embedding` entries:

```json
"url_suffix": {
  "chat": "chat/completions",
  "files": "files",
  "embedding": "embeddings/multimodal",
  "models": "models"
}
```

No new public API. No interface change. No factory change.

_No response_

```Markdown
No new docs are needed. VolcEngine is already in the model provider picker, with chat
and embedding already working. This issue just makes the existing model-list UI return
real data for VolcEngine instead of an error, the same way it already returns real
data for DeepSeek, Gitee, NVIDIA, OpenAI, and SiliconFlow.

  "input": ["text 1", "text 2"],

  "name": "text-embedding-v3",

  "model_types": ["embedding"]
}
```

This enhancement could be drawn from [Hierarchical Abstract Tree for Cross-Document Retrieval-Augmented
Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.00529), as well as from the following [sources](https://github.com/Newiz430/Psi-RAG):

### Actual behavior

Datasets configured with `permission = me` are intended to be private to the owner, but multiple document APIs authorize access using `KnowledgebaseService.accessible()`, which only checks whether the caller belongs to the dataset's tenant and does not enforce the dataset permission flag.

This creates an authorization bypass where a non-owner tenant member can access or modify a private dataset if they know its `dataset_id`.

Any tenant member with the `dataset_id` can pass authorization checks on several document endpoints because access is granted based on tenant membership rather than the dataset's permission setting.

This can expose private document inventories and may also allow unauthorized modification actions such as document deletion, metadata updates, or parse control operations.

### Expected behavior

Only the dataset owner should be able to access a dataset marked with `permission = me`. Tenant membership alone should not grant access to private datasets.

2. As User A, create a dataset with permission set to `me` so it is private.
3. Confirm User B cannot see this dataset through normal dataset listing.
4. As User B, obtain the private dataset's `dataset_id`.
5. Call a document API that checks `KnowledgebaseService.accessible()`, for example `GET /api/v1/datasets/<dataset_id>/documents`.
6. Observe that the request succeeds even though the dataset is marked private.

- Use a per-call context.WithTimeout (the existing nonStreamCallTimeout constant) so a slow embedding call cannot

    "models": "models",

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

```Markdown
Up front, so reviewers don't have to read the rest to find out: this isn't a bug report. Nothing here is broken at runtime. I noticed three spots while reading the file/document handling code where a `ThreadPoolExecutor` is created without a `with` block or an explicit `shutdown()` call, and I initially thought "that's a leak." It isn't — CPython cleans up the worker threads when the executor is GC'd, via the `_threads_queues` weakref + atexit machinery, so threads don't pile up across calls. I want to flag that explicitly so this doesn't get triaged as a vuln and dismissed.

What's left after stripping the false alarm is a code-hygiene ask. The lifecycles are harder to reason about than they need to be, and one of the three spots could just drop the executor entirely in favor of `asyncio.to_thread`.

The three spots:

- `api/db/services/file_service.py::get_files` (around lines 790–805) creates `exe = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=5)` and lets GC handle it.
- `api/db/services/file_service.py::parse_docs` (around lines 557–566) does the same with `max_workers=12`.
- `rag/svr/task_executor.py::do_handle_task` creates `executor = concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor()` near the top of the function (around line 1076) and shuts it down in `finally` with `executor.shutdown(wait=False)` (around line 1287). The executor is only ever used on one branch (standard chunking) and only ever receives a single task — `build_TOC`.

A couple of things that are worth ruling out, since they came up while I was looking at this:

- `executor.shutdown(wait=False)` in `task_executor.py` doesn't kill in-flight `build_TOC` work. Running tasks complete in their worker threads regardless of how shutdown is called. On the happy path `toc_thread.result()` is awaited before `finally` runs anyway, so there's nothing in flight at shutdown time. On cancellation/error paths the result is dropped, but build_TOC still finishes — which is what you want for cancellation.
- The default-sized executor in `task_executor.py` doesn't actually allocate threads up front; threads are created lazily on `submit()`. So branches that never reach the submit don't pay any cost.
```

### Describe the feature you'd like

Make the lifecycles explicit (or get rid of the executor when something simpler does the job). Concretely:

- `get_files` and `parse_docs` keep their executors but use `with ... as exe:` so cleanup is deterministic and exception-safe.
- `do_handle_task` drops the executor and uses `asyncio.to_thread` for `build_TOC`, since the surrounding function is already `async` and only one task ever runs through it.

### Describe implementation you've considered

For the two `file_service.py` functions it's a straight wrap-and-reindent — about 16 lines touched in `get_files` and ~10 in `parse_docs`, no behavior change. The existing `.result()` calls already happen before the executor would have been shut down, so the implicit `shutdown(wait=True)` at the end of the `with` block has nothing left to wait for.

For `do_handle_task` the clean version looks something like this:

```python
toc_thread = asyncio.create_task(
    asyncio.to_thread(build_TOC, task, chunks, progress_callback)
)
...
d = await toc_thread
```

That lets you delete the executor at line 1076 and the `executor.shutdown(wait=False)` in the `finally`. Net change is around 4 lines edited, 2 deleted; `import asyncio` is already ther

### RAGFlow workspace code commit ID

15dcdd7b5

### RAGFlow image version

nightly (main @ 15dcdd7b5)

### Other environment information

```Markdown
- Component: Python backend (Flask/Quart) — api/apps/document_app.py
- Affected endpoint: GET /v1/document/get/<doc_id>
- Auth decorator on route: @login_required only (no tenant scoping)
```

### Actual behavior

While reading through `api/apps/document_app.py` I noticed the `/get/<doc_id>` route is gated by `@login_required` and nothing else. It calls `DocumentService.get_by_id(doc_id)` (a global lookup, no tenant filter) and then streams the file straight from MinIO via `File2DocumentService.get_storage_address(...)` and `settings.STORAGE_IMPL.get(...)`. There's no check anywhere in between to confirm the document's KB actually belongs to the caller.

In practice this means any logged-in user — including a brand new self-serve signup — can download another tenant's document just by knowing the `doc_id`. It's the actual file content, not metadata.

What makes me fairly confident this is a real bug and not intentional: every other place in the codebase that resolves a document by id does enforce tenant scoping. The SDK route in `api/apps/sdk/doc.py` does `KnowledgebaseService.query(id=doc[0].kb_id, tenant_id=tenant_id)` right after `get_by_id`, and `api/apps/restful_apis/document_api.py` does the same at several call sites (around lines 174, 1156, 1796). The web-app route is the odd one out.

There's also already a helper for exactly this check — `DocumentService.accessible(doc_id, user_id)` in `api/db/services/document_service.py` — which joins through `UserTenant` so it also handles users who belong to multiple tenants / shared team KBs. So the fix can reuse existing code.

### Expected behavior

Hitting `GET /v1/document/get/<doc_id>` should only succeed when the caller actually has access to that document via their tenant/team membership. Otherwise it should return an authorization error rather than the file bytes.

### Steps to reproduce

```Markdown
1. Set up two accounts:
   - Tenant A: any logged-in user (a fresh signup is enough).
   - Tenant B: a separate tenant with at least one uploaded document. Note its doc_id (call it DOC_B).

2. From Tenant A's session, request Tenant B's document directly:

   curl -X GET "https://<host>/v1/document/get/<DOC_B>" \
     -H "Cookie: session=<TENANT_A_SESSION>" \
     --output leaked.bin

3. The response body contains Tenant B's file, even though Tenant A has no
   membership in Tenant B. doc_ids are UUID-shaped so they aren't trivially
   enumerable, but they do leak through logs, support tickets, screenshots,
   browser history, and other endpoints' responses.
```

### Additional information

Suggested fix — add an authorization check in `api/apps/document_app.py::get` after `DocumentService.get_by_id` and before the storage read. Either of these would work, but the first is closer to what the rest of the codebase does for documents:

```python
# Preferred — also handles shared/team KBs
if not DocumentService.accessible(doc_id, current_user.id):
    return get_data_error_result(message="No authorization.")
```

```python
# Minimum — matches the SDK pattern
if not KnowledgebaseService.query(id=doc.kb_id, tenant_id=current_user.id):
    return get_data_error_result(message="No authorization.")
```

It's probably worth a quick sweep of the other `@login_required` routes in the web-app blueprints for the same `get_by_

### RAGFlow workspace code commit ID

1d0519d02

### RAGFlow image version

main / nightly

### Other environment information

```Markdown
Affected layer: Go model provider layer
Affected files:
- internal/entity/models/ollama.go
- internal/entity/models/lmstudio.go
- internal/entity/models/vllm.go
```

### Actual behavior

Three of the Go model drivers leave CheckConnection as a stub that always returns an error:

  // ollama.go
  func (o *OllamaModel) CheckConnection(apiConfig *APIConfig) error {
      return fmt.Errorf("no such method")
  }

  // lmstudio.go
  func (m *LmStudioModel) CheckConnection(apiConfig *APIConfig) error {
      return fmt.Errorf("no such method")
  }

  // vllm.go
  func (z *VllmModel) CheckConnection(apiConfig *APIConfig) error {
      return fmt.Errorf("no such method")
  }

So when a tenant configures Ollama, LM Studio, or vLLM as a model provider in the Go layer and clicks "Check connection", they always get an error, even when the connection is fine and the host is reachable.

This is a real user-facing gap because Ollama in particular is one of the most popular local LLM runners, and LM Studio is a common companion. vLLM is widely used for self-hosted deployments. All three want a working connection check.

What makes this clearly a bug rather than a missing feature: all three drivers already have a working ListModels method that hits the /models endpoint with the configured base URL and API key. The "Check connection" path could simply reuse that.

Other Go drivers already follow this exact pattern:

  // moonshot.go, xai.go, deepseek.go, aliyun.go, gitee.go
  func (z *XAIModel) CheckConnection(apiConfig *APIConfig) error {
      _, err := z.ListModels(apiConfig)
      return err
  }

So the standard is set. ollama, lm-studio, and vllm are the three odd ones out.


### Expected behavior

CheckConnection on ollama, lm-studio, and vllm should call ListModels and return its error directly. If the API key is valid and the base URL is reachable, the check should succeed. If not, it should return whatever error the underlying HTTP call produced.

No new endpoint, no new dependency, no interface change. Just wire the existing pieces together.


### Steps to reproduce

```Markdown
1. In the Go layer, configure any of the three providers (ollama, lm-studio, vllm) with a real base URL and (where relevant) a real API key.
2. Click "Check connection" in the model provider UI.
3. Observe the request always fails with "no such method" regardless of the actual reachability of the upstream.
4. Compare with moonshot or xai under the same UI flow, where "Check connection" works.
```

### Additional information

_No response_
payload.title: [Bug]: Go drivers ollama, lm-studio, and vllm have CheckConnection stubbed despite working ListModels

At the same time, conf/models/zhipu-ai.json already lists a rerank model out of the box and already wires up the rerank URL suffix:

The SiliconFlow Go driver already implements Rerank against the same OpenAI-compatible /rerank shape, so the rest of the codebase is ready to call into the driver. ZhipuAI is the missing piece.
```

### Describe the feature you'd like

Implement ZhipuAIModel.Rerank in internal/entity/models/zhipu-ai.go so that the listed glm-rerank model works end to end.

The driver should:

- POST to /api/paas/v4/rerank on the same base URL the chat path uses, using the existing URLSuffix.Rerank from config.
- Accept a model name, a query string, and a list of candidate texts.
- Return a []float64 with one relevance score per text, in the same order the texts were given.
- Use the same HTTP client and the same shared transport that the chat path already builds.
- Use a per-call context deadline so a slow rerank call cannot block forever.

No new public API. No interface change. No factory change. Just a real implementation behind an existing method.


### Describe implementation you've considered

_No response_
